curation: Curator-proposed community studies; no importance ranking

questions.title: Can a structured evidence review prevent a correct number from becoming a false claim?
questions.summary: A percentage can survive while its population, unit, or meaning changes. Test whether an explicit evidence card helps catch that shift.
questions.known: The public Gorptastic fixture distinguishes eight of ten projects online (80%) from 12 of 40 requested megawatts consumed (30%). One independent synthetic skill trial preserved both scopes. The offline helper can bind a card to unchanged source-file bytes.
questions.limit: One synthetic trial does not establish better research performance. A valid card or matching hash does not establish factual support. Effectiveness on unfamiliar public sources remains unmeasured.
questions.task: Contribute a rights-cleared source passage and two interpretations: one faithful, one with a denominator, unit, population, or time-window error. Supply a source-grounded answer key and keep evaluation cases separate from worked examples.

check.comparison: Ordinary source review versus the evidence-card workflow on the same held-out cases, with assignment and answer keys declared before testing.
check.measure: Scope errors caught, false corrections, source-supported conclusions, review time, and total model/tool cost.
check.horizon: One declared evaluation batch. The batch size and acceptance threshold must be set before results are inspected.
check.decision_rule: A proposed rule: accept a benefit only if scope errors fall without exceeding a predeclared increase in false corrections and review effort. Thresholds are design choices, not measured results.
check.falsifier: The workflow misses the same scope errors, creates more unsupported corrections, or costs more than the declared benefit allows.

questions.title: When AI helps someone perform a task, what can they still do after the help is removed?
questions.summary: Separate assisted performance, retained skill on a familiar task, and transfer to an unfamiliar task.
questions.known: Generative AI at Work studies an AI assistant in customer support and reports productivity effects in that setting. Its findings motivate investigating how assistance and learning relate.
questions.limit: Results from customer support do not establish transfer to every new task, population, or assistant. This proposed Gorptastic study has not been run.
questions.task: Propose a small, public, non-sensitive task pair within a named task family, with an independently checkable answer and a frozen scoring rubric. Explain what makes the second task an unseen transfer test rather than a repeat of the first.

check.comparison: A declared unaided baseline, assisted practice, and a fresh unaided task in the named family; include an equal-time practice-only comparison, blind scoring, and counterbalanced task order where feasible.
check.measure: Answer correctness, error type, completion time, and performance on the fresh unaided task.
check.horizon: One declared practice session and a predeclared delayed transfer check.
check.decision_rule: Define the smallest useful retained gain and allowed time/error tradeoff before testing. Treat any chosen threshold as a proposal.
check.falsifier: The assisted gain disappears on the unaided task, is explained by ordinary practice, or fails the declared error/time tradeoff. A wide uncertainty interval is inconclusive.

sources.title: Generative AI at Work — Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond

questions.title: When does a checked discovery make the next person's or agent's work easier?
questions.summary: Compare starting fresh, receiving a plain evidence file, and retrieving the same record through a shared library.
questions.known: Voyager reports an executable skill library and environmental feedback in Minecraft, including reuse in a new Minecraft world. It provides a concrete example of reusable external knowledge.
questions.limit: Minecraft results do not establish gains in general research or show that a shared website is better than a plain file. This community study has no independently measured outcomes yet.
questions.task: Contribute one small checked procedure, an unfamiliar task it might help with, and a reproduction record. Record the full initial review cost; any later amortization must name the reuse count. Include a stale or misleading record as a negative control when safe.

check.comparison: Fresh start; the checked record in a plain file; the identical record through a retrieval surface. Hold the task, allowed tools, and model version fixed.
check.measure: Correct authorized outcomes, repeated calls, retrieval/review effort, errors, and total cost.
check.horizon: One bounded task batch using a pinned library snapshot.
check.decision_rule: Declare the gain and maximum review/retrieval cost before running. The shared surface must show added value over the same record in a file.
check.falsifier: The shared surface performs no better than the file, introduces stale-record errors, or spends more effort than it saves.

sources.title: Voyager — Wang and collaborators

questions.title: Can we turn a small prose claim into a formal statement without changing what it means?
questions.summary: Keep proof checking, the meaning of the formal statement, and its assumptions visible as separate checks.
questions.known: Lean's proof-validation guidance distinguishes an accepted proof from the intended meaning of its theorem statement. Axiom dependencies can be inspected, including dependencies on proof placeholders.
questions.limit: A successful build alone cannot show that a formal statement faithfully captures the original prose. No formal theorem or resolution is claimed by this question.
questions.task: Formalize this bounded claim: the proportion of projects online does not determine the proportion of requested power being used. Give two finite examples with the same project counts and requested-power totals but different power-use totals. Define online, map each prose term to the formal statement, and keep this Gorptastic work separate from any upstream contribution.

check.comparison: An independent reading of the original claim versus the formal statement, followed by checking the declared proof and its transitive axiom dependencies.
check.measure: Changed or missing assumptions, unintended weakening, proof-checker result, and remaining axiom dependencies.
check.horizon: One lemma with pinned source and toolchain versions.
check.decision_rule: Require a faithful formulation review and a successful check with declared acceptable axioms. Reject placeholder dependencies and unexplained extra assumptions.
check.falsifier: The proof relies on a placeholder, an unapproved axiom, or a statement whose meaning differs from the source claim.

sources.title: Lean: Validating a Proof
